conviction_note: The evidence is balanced: the Q3 NIM reset, the $20M lease loss and a 5% consensus cut were all put in public at Barclays on 2026-09-15 and are priced (stock about -13% since early September, MS downgrade 10-12). What is left is a more hawkish rate path than the curve Ally guided on, with Ally already lifting savings and CD rates, which threatens the 'exit above 3.7% NIM' language, set against benign big-bank consumer credit and a lowered bar. That gives p_up 48 on a 4.5% absolute move, and findings that sum to -0.5.
bar: Adjusted EPS about $1.32-1.34 and revenue $2.28-2.30B, NIM 3.6%: Zacks via Yahoo $1.32 / $2.28B / NIM 3.6%, cut 5% in 30 days (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ally-financial-ally-q3-earnings-121516056.html, 2026-10-15); Benzinga $1.33 and MarketBeat $1.34 (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-20-ally-financial-inc-stock/). Older aggregators showed $1.36-1.47 from before the cut (https://www.itiger.com/news/1168760375). Company guide: FY26 NIM ex-OID 3.6-3.7% with potential to exit above, retail auto NCO 1.8-2.0%, consolidated NCO 1.2-1.3%, average earning assets +3-5% (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/21/ally-ally-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). At Barclays 2026-09-15: Q3 NIM roughly flat q/q and about $20M of Stellantis lease losses (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/ally-financial-erwartet-im-q3-stagnierende-nim-wegen-stellantis-ruckrufen).
positioning_check: Short interest 12.93M shares, 4.26% of float, short ratio 4.05 days (Yahoo, settlement 2026-08-14). Fintel shows 4.76% / 6.82 days and Equibles 4.33% / 3.6 days, both undated (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ALLY/key-statistics/, https://fintel.io/s/us/ALLY). The short is not crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is +6.5 vol points, so downside is paid; put/call OI is 0.25. The event-implied move is 7.11% but only indicative (ATM spread 42% of mid). Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell); stock -8.9% over the past month, -5.72% over 20 days, -20.4% from its 52-week high and +4.6% above its 52-week low.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%. The minutes of 10-07 say most officials expect another hike by year-end, while Ally's FY26 NIM guide (3.6-3.7%, 'potential to exit above the high end') was built on a June-30 curve with one September hike and the next in early 2027. Ally has since raised its savings APY from 3.00% (09-24) to 3.10% (by 10-13) and lifted 8 CD rates on 09-22 (3-year 3.60% to 4.00%). Fifth Third said on 10-19 that deposit competition 'is heating up', and top online savings rates rose from 4.27% to 4.35% between 10-05 and 10-14. So the Q4 NIM exit language is at risk of being softened on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (NIM up, guide held or raised) +8.1%; Q2 2026 (EPS miss $1.21 vs $1.22-1.25, asset-growth guide raised) -2.39%. In Sept 2024 a mid-quarter credit and NIM warning cost about -17%. NIM and guide changes are what this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Morgan Stanley downgraded on exactly this funding-cost thesis on 10-12 (PT $55 to $43) and the stock is near its 52-week low. If the market fully expected a walk-back of the exit-above-3.7% NIM language, consensus NIM would sit below 3.6% and skew would be wider. Ally's own deposit-rate increases after the hike are not in the Zacks metric previews.

findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-15 the CFO guided Q3 NIM roughly flat q/q (Q2 NIM ex-OID 3.63%) instead of the sequential rise implied in July. He flagged about $20M of Q3 lease-residual losses from Stellantis PHEV recalls and held the FY NIM range. The bar has already absorbed this: consensus NIM is 3.6% and Q3 EPS was cut 5% in 30 days to $1.32.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: NIM +11bp q/q with an EPS miss, -2.39%. The pre-release on 09-15 coincided with the stock sliding from about $43 (early Sept) to $37.6.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, since it falls inside what the company told the market. Filed because a flat-NIM quarter with the lease loss already in consensus leaves only a small residual: if not priced, the Zacks NIM estimate would still read 3.7% and EPS would not have been cut 5%.
findings.independence: Barclays summary: https://quartr.com/events/ally-financial-inc-ally-barclays-24th-annual-global-financial-services-conference_3YFVGbMp. Reaffirmation recap 09-21: https://www.webull.com/news/15618471465665536. Both rest on the same 09-15 presentation.

findings.finding: Capital One's auto book, the closest monthly-disclosing peer, shows mixed credit. August 2026 auto NCO was 1.66% against 1.58% in August 2025, a year-over-year rise, while July was 1.48% against 1.59%. 30+ delinquency kept improving: 4.54% in August 2026 against 5.03% a year earlier. Manheim fell 1.1% m/m in September to 205.9 (-0.6% y/y), Cox called September depreciation steeper than usual and cut its 2026 forecast to +0.2% from +2%, which means higher loss severity. Ally's own Q2 retail auto 30+ DQ improvement had narrowed to 8bp y/y (4.80%). Ally's Q3 2025 retail auto NCO was 1.88% and its FY26 guide is 1.8-2.0%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit surprises have moved ALLY most: -17% in Sept 2024 on a July/August NCO warning, and a large drop on the Oct 2024 NCO guide raise. In 2026, with NCOs improving y/y, prints were +8.1% and -2.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: COF monthly auto metrics are public but rarely mapped to Ally. If the market were pricing a y/y NCO uptick at Ally, consensus would expect a retail auto NCO rise rather than continued improvement (the Barclays summary says improvement is expected in 2H). The CFO said on 09-15 that guidance was on track, so it was not alarmed. This is a proxy, not Ally's own number.

Ally Q2 DQ: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040729/000119312526309539/d40046dex991.htm.

findings.finding: Banks that reported Q3 2026 show benign consumer credit, which argues against a large reserve build or an NCO guide raise at Ally. JPMorgan's consumer reserve build was $50M against $575M a year earlier and its card NCO fell to 2.91% from 3.15%. Fifth Third reported consumer NCO of 0.52%, flat y/y, and 'credit quality remained stable' (10-19). US Bancorp NCOs were $523M against $536M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ally's provision and reserve build drove the Q2 2026 miss ($430M provision, CECL build on growth), which traded -2.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: Broad bank credit prints are seen by everyone, but Ally's stock fell over the same weeks they came out, so the market is not giving Ally credit for a benign consumer. If it were, ALLY would not be near its 52-week low with put skew. This is a proxy: prime bank consumer books, not Ally's nonprime-heavy auto mix.

findings.finding: The bar and the price have both been reset into the print. Consensus Q3 EPS was cut 5% in 30 days to $1.32 (Zacks Rank #5 Strong Sell). The stock is about -13% from $43.27 on 09-03 to $37.61 (-8.9% over the month) and trades below the $44.92 book value per share analysts expect. Short interest is not crowded at about 4.3% of float. Ally has beaten EPS in 7 of its last 8 quarters and resumed buybacks ($148M in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, coming off a weak tape with a beat, gave +8.1%. Q3 2025 gave +3.56%. Q2 2026 missed by about $0.01-0.04 and fell -2.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: Against it is the put skew of +6.5 vol points, which says the market pays for downside. The case for it is that the drawdown has an identified cause (the 09-15 NIM pre-release plus the Fed hike) that is already in the lowered EPS bar, so a print that simply holds the FY guide clears a reduced hurdle. If the market expected only an in-line print, the stock would not sit 20% below its high at a discount to book.
findings.independence: Price path: https://www.benzinga.com/stock/ALLY (Sep 3 $43.27); estimate cut and beat record: https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-20-ally-financial-inc-stock/; Q2 buybacks: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040729/000119312526309539/d40046dex991.htm.

findings.finding: The insurance segment should have had a light Q3 for weather. US H1 2026 catastrophe losses ran about 28% below the decadal average, and the season's first US hurricane landfall (Isaias, Cat 2 near Destin FL, $1-4.5B insured) came on 9-10 October, which falls in Q4. Ally's dealer-inventory insurance therefore probably carried light Q3 weather losses, against a consensus for insurance premiums of $373.7M (+3.5%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Insurance is small; Q2 2026 insurance pre-tax was $53M GAAP / $24M core and did not drive the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small for anyone to model. The Isaias Q4 loss may get a mention on the call. This is a proxy and the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Ally issued $750M of 5.525% fixed-to-floating senior notes due 2030 on 2026-09-09/16, against its 6.848% notes due 2030 issued in Dec 2023. The money funds the raised asset-growth guide (+3-5%) at a lower unsecured spread, so this is routine funding of growth, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of financing items moving the print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced and neutral. Filed because the question 'what does the money buy' has an answer: balance-sheet growth that the company already guided up.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly negative, which agrees with the +6.5 put skew. The negative 20-day run-up and the 5% consensus cut cut the other way (a lowered bar), so they roughly offset and p_up sits at 48.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (sign against skew): the positioning/lowered-bar long shrunk from +1.0 to +0.6, because the put skew is +6.5 and I can only partly say why the options market is wrong.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Barclays NIM-flat/lease-loss finding moved from -0.3 to -0.2; it is inside what the company told the market.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): COF/Manheim credit moved from -0.5 to -0.4, broad bank credit from +0.5 to +0.4 and insurance weather from +0.2 to +0.1; all kept, sized as proxies.
Rule 4 (financing): the notes issue was already signed 0 after asking what it buys (the raised asset-growth guide).
p_up moved from 50 to 48 because the residual negative (the rate path against the guide curve) rests on Ally's own deposit-rate actions while the positives are proxies or positioning.
